comparison: Both evaluate claims about Ucn3 as an early marker of de-differentiation (C7, C29-C43, C97-C100). OpenEval finds the data SUPPORTED with clear evidence from immunostaining and qRT-PCR across multiple models. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting more detailed temporal analysis and criticizing the mixing of three diabetic models. Reviewers state the correlation with severity is 'not sufficient to support de-differentiation' and want individual disease data.

Both evaluate the S961 reversible diabetes model claims (C44-C51, C56-C58, C108). OpenEval finds the temporal dynamics and reversibility data SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and time course data. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the model but requesting more comprehensive quantitative temporal profiling of multiple markers at different time points during both de-differentiation and re-differentiation.

Both evaluate the transplantation experiment demonstrating reversibility (C59-C63). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by fluorescence imaging, qRT-PCR, and GSIS data. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, stating the GSIS data showing reduced glucose response is 'not sufficient to prove de-differentiation' and requesting additional molecular characterization of β cell gene expression in the culture system.

Both evaluate the screening results identifying Alk5 inhibitor II (C64, C67-C69). OpenEval finds the screening approach SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and statistical thresholds. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED, focusing their concerns on downstream functional validation rather than questioning the screening methodology itself.

Both evaluate Alk5 inhibitor II effects on gene expression recovery in 804G cells (C72-C76). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical significance. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on the extent of recovery compared to healthy controls and requiring immunohistochemistry confirmation of Ucn3 restoration.

Both acknowledge the limitation that gene expression recovery does not restore GSIS function (C77). OpenEval rates the overall result SUPPORTED while explicitly noting this limitation. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED, accepting the negative functional result and discussing its implications for clinical significance.

Both evaluate protective effects against cytokine-induced de-differentiation (C79-C83). OpenEval finds the gene expression data SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical reporting. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting functional validation through GSIS assays to confirm the protective effect extends beyond gene expression to function.

Both address the lack of GSIS recovery (C84). OpenEval acknowledges this limitation while rating the gene expression protection as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also accept this negative result as SUPPORTED, noting the clinical significance is unclear without functional restoration.

Both evaluate Alk5 inhibitor effects in diabetic mouse islets (C85-C90). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by qRT-PCR data showing gene expression induction even in severely diabetic islets. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting in vivo functional validation through administration to T2D mice to demonstrate restoration of GSIS or blood glucose improvement.

Both evaluate human islet data (C91, C113). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED though notes the limitation of single donor data. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns, accepting the demonstration of activity in human tissue as addressing translational relevance.

Both evaluate the proposed mechanistic model (C123-C128). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN, noting the model is plausible but largely speculative without direct mechanistic validation. Peer reviewers also rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting discussion of mechanism and physiological significance, and noting concerns about SMAD7's role in proliferation that may complicate the model.

Both evaluate preliminary negative results from systemic Alk5 inhibitor administration (C130). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as appropriate reporting of negative preliminary data highlighting need for β cell-specific targeting. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED, accepting the negative result while requesting proper in vivo functional studies in T2D mice.

OpenEval finds background and literature-based claims (C1-C5, C11-C24, C92-C96) SUPPORTED as providing appropriate context with well-cited references. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background claims specifically.

OpenEval finds claims about Ucn3 characterization and biology (C6, C25-C28, C101-C107) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations to previous literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims about Ucn3 as a maturity marker.
